# Background

- Heatwaves are projected to massively increase in duration and intensity by the end of the century

- Plasticity: an individual's ability to alter behavior or physiology in response to changes in their environment without genetic changes

- Acclimation: Short-term and often reversible sub-type of plasticity, two main parameters are **capacity** and **rate of acclimation**, which we understand to be inverse in many species

- *Skistodiaptomus pallidus* is a widespread freshwater calanoid copepod

# Questions

1.  How does acclimation capacity compare across populations?
2.  Is there a relationship between acclimation capacity and rate of acclimation across populations?

## Hypotheses

1.  The acclimation capacity will be higher in the population with a higher average surface temperature.
2.  The acclimation capacity and rate of acclimation will have a negative relationship.

# Results

```{r message = F, warning = F, echo=F}

ctmax_data = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/ctmax_data.csv")

acc_params = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/acc_params.csv")

contrasts = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/contrasts.csv")

library(tidyverse)

```

```{r standard-plot, out.width='90%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='CTmax (°C) over time (Acclimation hours) for the control (blue) and warm (red) treatments and CP and OP', fig.height=5}

#| label: fig-ctmax

ctmax_data %>% 
  filter(ctmax > 34) %>% 
  mutate(acc_hours = acc_hours + 0.1) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = acc_hours, y = ctmax, colour = treatment)) + 
  facet_grid(pop ~ .) +
  geom_point(size = 2) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ log(x)) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("control" = "royalblue",
                                 "warming" = "brown2")) + 
  labs(
    x = "Acclimation Hour", 
    y = "CTmax (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom", 
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r standard-plot, out.width='90%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='Graph of the model contrasts (Warming - Control; °C) over time (Acclimation Day) for CP and OP', fig.height=5}
#| label: fig-acclimation-parameters


param_data = contrasts %>%
  group_by(pop) %>% 
  arrange(acc_day) %>% 
  mutate(acc_day = if_else(acc_day == 0, 0.01, acc_day)) 

cp_params = filter(acc_params, pop == "CP")
op_params = filter(acc_params, pop == "OP")

# Create a new data frame with predicted values
acc_day <- seq(0, max(param_data$acc_day), length.out = 100)
cp_pred <- cp_params$z_asymp*(1-exp(-cp_params$lambda*acc_day))
op_pred <- op_params$z_asymp*(1-exp(-op_params$lambda*acc_day))

predictions = data.frame(acc_day, 
                         cp_pred, 
                         op_pred) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(cp_pred:op_pred), 
               names_to = c("pop", NA), 
               names_sep = "_", 
               values_to = "pred") %>% 
  mutate(pop = toupper(pop))

param_data %>% 
  drop_na(estimate) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = acc_day, y = estimate)) + 
  facet_wrap(pop~.) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_hline(data = acc_params, aes(yintercept = z_asymp),
             colour = "grey") + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - SE, ymax = estimate + SE), 
                linewidth = 1, width = 0.3) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  geom_line(data = predictions, aes(x = acc_day, y = pred),
            colour = "blue",
            linewidth=1.5)+
  labs(x = "Acc. Day", 
       y = "Contrast (Warming - Control; °C)") + 
  theme_bw(base_size = 24) + 
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom")

```

# Conclusion

- Capacity and rate of acclimation are negatively correlated

- Populations differ in both capacity and acclimation

- Ability to cope with global warming might depend on capacity and rate of acclimation

## Next Steps

- Replicate with two more populations of *S. pallidus*

- Room for a secondary project exploring the molecular underpinnings of these results
